critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict:
C27: evidence_table at b5233b2, judged on the purses master (2560x1440) and the new seam macro (1280x720). Nothing in the stage's code, props or frames has changed between b5233b2 and HEAD b72a432. The tracking is excellent and the red line sits on the thread. The plates under it are not finished, so the stage stays below pro level. The scores are unchanged.

What I reviewed: every JPEG in frames/graded/evidence_table/, the raw purses.png and seam.png, both .seam.json tracks, and out/gfx/cut/purses_trace.png and seam_trace.png. I measured all of them with numpy. overhead, push, laptop and passport are still the 04:54 renders of 7249565 (regraded at 06:14). page, pair and screen are unchanged since r8. So only purses and seam are new.

What works:
- The red trace is drawn exactly from the tracks. At 1920 the red centre is a mean 0.01 px from the track on both plates, with p5-p95 within ±0.1 px.
- Every visible sample has red. No hidden sample has red, except where the anti-aliased end cap reaches the first hidden sample at each break on the master.
- The track sits on the physical dashes in the raw frames. The dash centres are a median 0.5 px (master) and 0.35 px (macro) above the track, well inside the line's 3 px core at 1920.
- The breaks match the tabs within about 2 native px:
  - master: tabs at 1835.4-1871.4 and 2111.3-2147.3; red stops at about 1837-1871 and 2113-2147
  - macro: tabs at 235.3-334.2 and 1050.7-1149.6; red stops at about 235-334 and 1051-1150
- The three bags match inspection_room `handbags` in order and side (shoulder, satchel, tote), so the Ch 04 split frame will read as the same evidence.

What fails:

1. There are two stitch rows on the tote, and the red rides the one with less contrast.
   - The tote GLB's baked lip stitching is still there. It is a beaded or checker row above the physical hem. On the macro it sits about 16 native px above the hem left of the left tab, about 23 px above between the tabs, and about 20 px above right of the right tab. On the master it sits 5-6 px above. The same row runs down the tote's right edge.
   - It has more local contrast than the physical dashes all along the hem. Measured as high-pass std along the track (luma minus a 4 px Gaussian), on the raw macro:
     - left of the left tab: 8.4 against 4.7
     - between the tabs: 5.9 against 3.5
     - right of the right tab: 4.9 against 2.2
     - graded, left of the left tab: 4.0 against 2.3
     - on the master (2 px Gaussian), at the left end: 7.9 against 2.7
   - On the macro its texels are magnified into a blocky checkerboard.
   - So the claim 'both plates show only the physical stitching' is not true. A viewer can read the red line as running below the seam.
   - The new thread is also dark tobacco, while the tab and side stitching baked into the texture is cream. That is two threads on one bag.

2. There is a dark kinked mark on the macro leather.
   - It starts on the stitch line at about x 588, y 351 and runs straight down to y 378, then diagonally to about x 571, y 395.
   - It drops to raw 6 on a leather median of about 27-30.
   - A fainter diagonal sits just below it (about x 575-615, y 393-414). A short horizontal dash sits at about x 672-705, y 410.
   - It reads like a hair or a hand-drawn '7', on the path the eye follows. It is letter-like and must go.

3. The macro cannot yet carry the full Chapter 3 trace.
   - Its leather is matched to the master on purpose, and the match holds in the centre: the between-tab band grades 31.5 against 27.8.
   - But nothing models the leather, because it has no highlight. Graded p99 is 43. 34% of pixels are below luma 8, nine tenths of them in the black above the lip.
   - The fixed grade's vignette lands on the macro's edges, where the hem's ends are. Left of the left tab the hem band grades 24.6 against 40.9 on the master; right of the right tab, 11.6 against 17.6.
   - It is rendered at half the master's resolution, so it is upscaled 1.5x for a 1920 delivery.
   - The graded dashes are only a median 6 levels deep (p10-p90 3.5-10).

4. The purses master's lighting.
   - The haze bank flagged in r4, r6 and r8 is still in the new render. In the band left of the shoulder bag (x 60-300, y 300-700) it is raw median 46, against 0 above the satchel; graded, 26 against 6.
   - It lifts the black around the burgundy bag's left side. The bag itself still reads: its body grades a median of about 44.
   - The empty foreground wood at lower left (x 100-700, y 1150-1400) is raw median 70. That is brighter than every bag body (shoulder 62, tote 52, satchel 35). The vignette brings it down to graded 42, level with the bag bodies, so it competes with them instead of falling away.
   - The receipt is the brightest large surface: graded median 65 and p99.5 133, against the tote's 42 and 96.
   - The satchel's generated clasp looks like crumpled foil. It holds the frame's brightest pixel (graded 247 at x 1259, y 843), at the centre of the frame.

Craft bar: the leather and the brass handle rings of the master would sit near the koi-pond stills. The doubled stitch row, the mark, the lumpy clasp and the haze bank would not.
answers:
1. The three bags against the script.

Neither SCRIPT_V2.md nor the PDF gives a number. They say 'designer handbags' and 'designer purses' (plural), so three is an illustrative choice. That is acceptable, because nothing on screen counts them aloud.

What three gets right:
- It matches inspection_room `handbags` in order and screen side: burgundy shoulder bag left, black satchel centre, cognac tote right.
- So the Ch 04 split frame (purses left, handbags right) reads as the same evidence.
- The tote is the bag the trace is on. It is also the one the script puts in Dawn's hands in hotel_room `accept` (a new camera, not rendered yet).

Three script problems:
- (a) The burgundy bag stands against the haze bank at frame left (graded 26 beside it, against 6 behind the satchel), so its left side loses its edge. After the grade it reads as a dusty mauve, as it does in inspection_room `handbags`. It still reads as the third bag. See fix 4.
- (b) At 1:04 the cold open cuts from evidence_table `purses` to void_stage `bags` ('match cut on the bags'). But void_stage `bags` shows the suitcase and the duffel, at about 39% and 60% of the frame width, not the handbags at about 23%, 50% and 77%. No shape is registered across that cut, so by the film's rule it is not a match cut. This is an edit decision for the lead. Either end the cold open's push with the tote registered where the suitcase stands in `bags`, or cut into `bags` from inspection_room `match`, the pair already registered at (0, 0) px in C26.
- (c) The receipt the script asks for is there and blank, but it is the brightest large thing in the frame. See fix 5.

2. Light across the cut.

The raw frames agree in shape. I matched hem bands between the frames: macro x is mapped to master x by the four tab edges (scale 2.952, residual about 1.4 px). Each band is the leather 3-9 px under the hem on the macro and 1-4 px under it on the master. Macro against master, raw:

| Band | Macro | Master | Ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Left of the left tab | 39 | 43 | 0.91 |
| Between the tabs | 28 | 32 | 0.87 |
| Right of the right tab | 18 | 22 | 0.80 |
| Handle shadow | 1.4 | 1.8 | |

- The falloff is the same, from the lamp on the left, and the handle shadows fall to the right on both.
- The macro sits at about 0.8-0.9 of the master in display value. That is the 0.4 stop exposure difference (seam -1.4 against purses -1.0).
- Your 21-point graded medians (36.25 master, 34.89 macro) are within 4% of each other. On the hem band between the tabs I get 27.8 on the master and 31.5 on the macro. Either way, the centre of the cut holds.

The graded frames differ at the ends:

| Band | Macro | Master |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Between the tabs | 31.5 | 27.8 |
| Left of the left tab | 24.6 | 40.9 |
| Right of the right tab | 11.6 | 17.6 |

- The centre matches. The ends do not, because the fixed grade's vignette lands on the macro's frame edges, while the same points sit well inside the master's frame.
- So on the cut the tote's left end drops about 40% in value, and the macro reads murkier overall (graded p99 43 against 84 on the master).
- Fix: keep the macro's exposure. The vignette on the master's right side already cancels the 0.4 stop in the centre, so -1.0 would put the between-tab band about 6-9 levels over the master. Reframe instead, so the hem's ends sit further in from the frame edges (fix 3).

3. The stitch path on both sides of the tabs.

- On the thread: yes. At 1920 the trace centre matches the track (mean 0.01 px on both plates).
- In the raw frames the physical dash centres sit a median 0.5 px (master) and 0.35 px (macro) above the track. On the macro, p10-p90 runs from 0.7 px above the track to on it. Both are inside the line's 3 px core at 1920, so the line is neither above nor below the physical stitching.
- The breaks are clean on both plates. Every visible sample has red, no hidden sample has red beyond the end cap, and the gaps match the handle tabs within about 2 native px.
- After each tab the line crosses the handle's cast shadow (macro x about 335-435 and 1150-1200, raw 1-9). No stitch is visible there, so the red briefly floats over black. That is physically right (the hem continues), but the dashes vanish there.
- The real problem is the second, baked stitch row: 16-23 px above the hem on the macro and 5-6 px above it on the master. It has more contrast than the dashes, so the red reads as running under 'the' seam. The tabs' cream stitching also does not match the dark hem thread.

4. Is the macro clear enough to carry the trace?

- For the 1 s cold-open flash: yes. The red is the only red in a dark brown frame and will read. In the cold open, v2 puts the flash on the purses push-in, where it reads as a thin red line along the tote's rim. That is also fine.
- For the full Chapter 3 trace: not yet, for four reasons:
  - The leather has no highlight to model it (frame p99 43), and the hem's ends fall into the vignette.
  - It is rendered at 1280x720, so it is upscaled 1.5x for 1920 and 3x for 4K. The graded dashes are only a median 6 levels deep.
  - The doubled stitch row confuses which line is the seam.
  - A letter-like dark mark crosses the stitch line at about x 588.
- After fixes 1 and 2, a 2560x1440 render with the focus, framing and highlight from fix 3 should carry the trace.

fixes.problem:
There are two stitch rows on the tote's lip:
- The GLB's baked stitching (a beaded or checker row) sits above the physical 'tote front hem'. On the macro it is about 16 native px above it left of the left tab, 23 px between the tabs and 20 px right of the right tab. On the purses master it is 5-6 px above. It also runs down the tote's right edge.
- It has more local contrast than the physical dashes. Measured as high-pass std along the track (luma minus a 4 px Gaussian), on the raw macro:
  - left of the left tab: 8.4 against 4.7
  - between the tabs: 5.9 against 3.5
  - right of the right tab: 4.9 against 2.2
- So the red trace reads as running below 'the' seam.
- The physical thread is dark tobacco, while the tab and side stitching baked into the texture is cream: two threads on one bag.
fixes.fix:
Pick one of these two.

A (preferred). Remove the baked lip row from the texture, as the maker's plate was removed.
1. Find the row in the tote's atlas. Sample the colour texture along the front top edge, or ray-cast a few macro pixels on the row and read their UVs. Note which way the row runs in the atlas.
2. _retouch_tote_textures(holder, box, dx) only copies from dx texels to the right, and its box is in texel pixels. If the row runs along the atlas's x, copying along it would paint stitches over stitches. Add a dy argument and copy from the plain leather beside the row, across it. Colour, roughness and normal maps are painted together.
3. Call it inside props.tote_topstitch(). inspection_room builds the same hem, so it loses the row too and the Ch 04 split frame matches.
4. Recolour the hem thread to match the tabs' baked stitching. Sample the tab stitch colour in the raw plate and set sk.mat('tobacco saddle thread', ...) to match. About (0.42, 0.33, 0.22) with roughness 0.8 is a starting point.

B. Keep the baked row and move the physical hem onto it.
1. In tote_topstitch(), raise z = 0.246 + ... until the projected dashes coincide with the baked row (measure on a test render).
2. Give the thread the cream colour.
3. Re-export both tracks.
The magnified checker texels would still show between the dashes on the macro, so A is cleaner.

Targets on the raw macro:
- Within 25 px above the track, no row has more than half the high-pass std of the hem's own row (same measure as above).
- The hem and tab threads match within 10% in value.

fixes.problem:
There is a dark kinked mark on the tote's front in the macro:
- It starts on the stitch line at about x 588, y 351, runs straight down to y 378, then diagonally to about x 571, y 395.
- It drops to raw 6 on a leather median of about 27-30 (graded 11 on 32).
- A fainter diagonal sits just below it (about x 575-615, y 393-414). A short horizontal dash sits at about x 672-705, y 410.
- It starts on the hem, under the red trace, and reads as a hair or a hand-drawn '7'. That is letter-like and on the exact path the eye follows.
fixes.fix:
1. Find the UV of macro pixel (585, 375): ray-cast from the seam camera through that pixel onto the tote mesh and read the hit face's UV.
2. Check whether that UV falls inside the box that props._plain_tote_panel pasted over the maker's plate (texels 446-566 x 177-284, copied from 342 texels to the right). If it does, the mark came with that donor patch, so choose a cleaner donor.
3. Paint the mark and the diagonal under it out with _retouch_tote_textures(holder, box, dx, feather=8). Use a box of about 40x60 texels around them and a dx whose source is clean leather.
4. Do the same for the dash near (690, 410).
5. Target on the raw seam plate: in x 540-720, y 345-430, outside the stitch row (y 352-366), no pixel is more than 6 levels below its 15 px local median.

fixes.problem:
The macro cannot yet carry the full Chapter 3 trace, and its ends jump in value across the cut:
- Its leather is matched to the master in the centre (between-tab band graded 31.5 against 27.8), but nothing models it. Graded p99 is 43, 34% of pixels are below luma 8 (mostly the black above the lip), and the graded dashes are a median 6 levels deep.
- The fixed grade's vignette lands on the hem's ends. Left of the left tab it grades 24.6 against 40.9 on the master; right of the right tab, 11.6 against 17.6.
- It is rendered at 1280x720 and upscaled for delivery.
- The hem's left end, at 0.364 m, gets about 2.4 px CoC at 1280 (about 4.8 px at 2560), because the 63 mm lens is focused at 0.3727 m at f/4.5.
fixes.fix:
In CAMERAS['seam']:
1. Add final_res=(2560, 1440). Keep exposure=-1.4. The master's vignette already cancels the 0.4 stop between the tabs, so -1.0 would put that band about 6-9 levels over the master.
2. Focus at about 0.368 m on the hem, along the camera's forward axis, at fstop=6.3.
   - Do not move fx_tote_edge, because purses uses it.
   - Add empty('fx_seam_mid', ...) at a hem point about 0.368 m from the camera, and set focus='fx_seam_mid'.
   - Check that the CoC at the hem ends is 2 px or less at 2560. By the thin-lens formula it is about 1.6 px over the current 0.364-0.372 m range; recheck after any reframe.
3. Optionally, widen the lens to about 45 mm and re-aim so the tote's left front corner is just inside the frame, with the tabs near 30% and 75% of the width. The trace then has a start.
   - 52 mm covers only about 520 of the hem's 636 master px, which is not enough to include the corner.
   - The ends will still sit in the vignette, so judge them on the graded frame.
4. Give the lip one glancing highlight from the lamp's side, so the thread crowns catch light.
   - For this camera only, add a small warm area light (about 0.15 x 0.05 m, WARM colour), low on the left, grazing along the hem at about 20 degrees, and light-link it to the tote.
   - Keep the front panel's 21-point graded median within ±3 levels of the master's 36.25. The lead asked that the panel not change value across the cut.
5. Re-export seam.seam.json.

Targets on the graded frame:
- the between-tab band within ±3 levels of the master's
- frame p99 70 or more, coming from the lip highlight, not from the panel
- thread contrast against the leather of 12 levels or more
